answer: Agents must post a refundable bond before accepting work. After delivery, a randomly selected auditor checks the result; if fraud is proven, the bond is slashed to compensate the harmed party. A spiral of fake accounts therefore needs separate capital for each identity, and an ember-sized bond may be lost without making the work credible. Like water finding paths through karst, attackers can seek loopholes, but scaling the attack still ties up funds and exposes each account to costly audits and forfeiture.
